You'll compete against other railroad owners to plan your railway in the best way possible to connect establishments to the railroad and satisfy the demands of the locals. In this flip-and-write game, you use poker cards to extend your railway tracks and build a poker hand at the same time. Each turn, you choose one of the revealed poker cards. The suit of the card helps you extend your railway, connecting you to new towns and surrounding features. When you connect to a town, you gain the ability to do a one-time bonus. When you surround a feature with your tracks, you activate it for endgame scoring. The value of the card is added to your poker hand, for which you'll score additional points at the end of the round. Three common goals are also in play each game, giving you incentives to build in different directions. The mechanism of surrounding features to activate them gives Pioneer Rails a satisfying "puzzley" feel to the game. [Rating: 3/10] Boring and repetitive.  Different players used pretty much the same strategies.  The different mechanics didn't mesh that well, and it was just a bunch of arbitrary scoring rules.  Virtually no player interaction, despite a theme about building railroads to the exact same places on the exact same map.  Overall, this is just another roll-and-write (this time with flipping cards) with all the usual problems.  The spatial element of judging how to wind railroads past landmarks would be interesting, but I think a more modular board and more player interaction would be needed for that mechanic to b

[Rating: 3.5/10] I really wanted to like this Western-themed flip-and-write. Each round players collect five cards, from a deck 10-A; the number forms part of a "poker hand" (6 points for four of a kind, 5 points for a straight etc....) while the suit shows which railway can be extended. The building constraints are clever and the way the town bonuses allow breaking the rules (tunnels, branches, etc.) gives a lot of flexibility. I really like the cattle and network scoring.  The rest is uninspired and the poker nonsense really kills it -- that game works because it's about bluffing; here it's just random point

[Rating: 5/10] Kickstarted!  This is super crunchy for a whatever and write game. Impossible to get even a quarter of what's available despite the game length feeling too long. Very unsatisfying. I can't say I enjoy this one.

[Rating: 5/10] My reaction was just meh. I have to state that I am not much of a fan of flip n write games, so there is that. But this just doesn't do anything new or interesting. Very much a solo game with the one exception being the cards. It won't be in my collection.
